_doc: The baseline for CON-OP-16: maintenance effort per stable unit of landscape, while burden indicators hold steady. Fixed before any comparison is run (docs/50_process/520_record-keeping.md, 'The maintenance baseline comes before the second source'). Every figure below is computable from the files in records/. Drafted by claude-opus-5-5 at S06-048; reviewed by sol and astra (XREV_2026-09-25_maintenance-baseline_*); revised at S06-060 with the author's accepted findings 1-7; the numbers in 'tolerances' are proposals for the author to set.

epoch._doc: The reporting window. The landscape grows one source at a time, so the natural window is the interval between two source acquisitions, not a calendar period.
epoch.definition: Epoch n runs from the step that acquires the n-th source (sources.jsonl acquired_by) up to, not including, the step that acquires source n+1. The last epoch is open until the post-mortem.
epoch.calendar_companion: Each epoch also reports its elapsed calendar days, so that a long epoch is not mistaken for a costly one.
epoch.stock_served: Each maintenance step is charged to the stock existing at that step, not to the epoch's end stock (sol 3).
epoch.comparable: Only closed epochs are compared, and only once every refresh that fell due in them has an outcome (sol 3).

service_commitment._doc: Replaces the once-per-epoch refresh rule (sol 2). Intervals are ours, not the publisher's, so the sandbox does not drown in refreshes.
service_commitment.rule: Each refresh that falls due is recorded as done or missed. A missed refresh is a broken service commitment and counts as burden. Refresh, check re-runs and repairs are maintenance.

stable_units._doc: The denominator. Counted at the start of each epoch from assets.jsonl and sources.jsonl, status supported only. Kept as separate counts, never combined into one index.

primary.name: supported_sources
primary.count: sources with status acquired whose assets include at least one supported source-file

secondary.name: supported_assets_by_kind
secondary.count: assets with status supported, per kind: source-file, table, model, report, control

secondary.name: service_commitments
secondary.count: supported sources under the refresh rule above

stable_units.excluded: Steps, tickets, commits, documents and review notes are not stock; counting them would reward fragmentation (sol, XREV maintenance-share finding 8).
stable_units.eligible: A source counts as stock only after it has passed its acceptance checks and survived one full refresh (sol 4, astra 2).
stable_units.dependencies: Counted as burden, never as stock: counting them as stock would reward coupling (sol 4).

effort._doc: The numerator, reported as separate measures and never summed. Classification is the step's work_class, decided by the counterfactual: would this be needed merely to keep the existing landscape running?

classes_counted.build: reported alongside, for the share as a diagnostic
classes_counted.rework: charged to the class of the step it corrects, following rework_of to the first non-rework step
classes_counted.overhead: reported separately as the apparatus share (PRC-OP-2); in neither numerator nor denominator

effort.rebuilds: Replacing an existing asset is maintenance unless it delivers a capability that is separately valued and recorded (XREV maintenance-share finding 2).

author: responses (unique response_id)
words
large acts
measures.elapsed: sum of ts_end minus ts where both are exact; otherwise unknown, never zero

effort.displaced_effort: Work the author does outside the conversation for the landscape is recorded as an H act step or it does not exist; the refresh rule makes such acts visible when they are needed.

burden_indicators._doc: What must hold steady while effort per unit is judged. Absolute values and per-unit values are both reported (XREV maintenance-share finding 5).
burden_indicators.defect_backlog_age_days: age of the oldest open defect and median age of open defects at the end of each epoch
burden_indicators.failed_or_unresolved_checks: check steps whose last run on an asset failed or ended partial, not superseded by a later passing check on the same asset
burden_indicators.stale_assets: supported source-files whose data_as_of is older than their publisher's cadence allows at the epoch start
burden_indicators.pending_on_author: steps with outcome pending and blocker human-wait at the epoch end

tolerances._doc: Set provisionally by the author at S06-052; revised after review. Indicative, not significance tests.
tolerances.effort_per_unit_flat: Kept as a separate acceptance check only: from the third epoch on, maintenance per unit of workload stays within +10% of the second epoch.
tolerances.burden_steady: Open weighted defects per supported source stay within +25% of the second epoch, and no high or critical defect is older than one epoch.
tolerances.hard_fail: Demoted to a trigger for investigation, not a verdict (astra 3): an epoch in which maintenance steps outnumber build steps while burden rises is examined by hand. No budget is set for collapse; the author ruled none for now.
tolerances.no_redefinition: These definitions may not change after the second source is acquired. A change needs a new baseline file, the old one kept as superseded, and every result reported under both.
tolerances.test: Across successive closed epochs, maintenance effort grows no faster than the workload maintained, while burden stays steady (astra 1). Judged on the trend of effort-to-workload ratios, per effort measure.

limits: The author's effort is a proxy (responses, words, large acts) by his ruling; it is not time.
The agent's token use is not observable; tool calls stand in for it.
Sandbox users and business stakeholders are simulated (ADR-0012), so displaced effort to other people cannot occur and cannot be measured.

Comparison at fixed capacity (XREV maintenance-share finding 7) is approximated by one author and one recording model throughout; a change of model mid-sandbox must be recorded and results split at it.
ruling: Provisional. The author: "let's try it for now. maybe do pass past sol and astra." Definitions may still change on review until the second source is acquired; after that, the no_redefinition tolerance applies. Revised 2026-09-25 after review; the author: "let's not make it too serious yet, we're still putting our feelers out. No budget in 8. I'll go with 1-7."

workload._doc: The denominator that matters (astra 1 and 2). Recorded by the machinery at each acquisition and refresh, per source.
descriptors: rows changed since the previous refresh
workload.rule: Effort is related to workload per source and per refresh, not to a count of sources. Shared maintenance, not attributable to one source, is reported separately.

classification_guard._doc: Takes the key judgement out of the recorder's hands (sol 1).
classification_guard.rule: A step whose trigger is refresh or check-failure, or which modifies an asset that existed before the current epoch began, is maintain (or rework of maintenance). Enforced by tools/check_repo.py through the step fields trigger and assets_modified.
classification_guard.unenforced: That a relabelled step keeps its first classification is not checked mechanically; git history shows relabelling.
